entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Petitioner claims to be the owner of the land bearing R.S. No.128/1 measuring 5 acres situated at Gadag.

The petitioner submitted an application under Section 95 of the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964 (hereinafter referred to as "Act" for short) seeking conversion of the entire extent of land for industrial purpose, which was acceded to by the competent authority.

2. The respondent No.2 issued a notification under Section 15 of the Karnataka Highways Act, 1964,
published in the official gazette on 13.11.2012 proposing to acquire 32 guntas 8 anas out of the entire extent of land.
The petitioner consented for acquisition of the land, and the respondent No.3 fixed the market value of the acquired land at Rs.874/- per square feet by treating it as commercial land.

Thereafter, the petitioner executed an agreement on 13.11.2013 consenting for acquisition of the subject land, and as per the terms of the agreement, the petitioner agreed to receive the total sum of Rs.9,51,786/- per gunta towards the compensation and other statutory benefits.

Though the agreement was executed on NC: 2024:KHC-D:3571 13.11.2013, the respondent No.2 passed the consent award on 26.08.2019 determining the total amount of compensation payable to the petitioner at Rs.4,25,04,279/- by treating it as a residential land, although the land was treated as commercial land by the respondent No.3 and an agreement was executed by the petitioner agreeing to receive the compensation by treating it as commercial land.

3. Learned Counsel for the Petitioner argued that the consent award passed treating the acquired land as residential land is contrary to the conversion order and also the order passed by respondent No.3 fixing the market value treating the acquired land as commercial land.

4. Learned AGA for the State submits that the consent award indicated that the subject land is converted for the residential purpose, and the respondent No.2 taking into consideration the conversion order has rightly determined the market value by treating it as residential land, and therefore, the consent award passed by the respondent No.2 is in conformity with the provisions of the law, and the same does not warrant interference.

sentences.text: Considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties.
6. Annexure - C is the order dated 25.11.2013 passed by the respondent No.3 by which the subject land is treated as commercial land, and the market value is fixed at Rs.874/- per square feet.

In light of the order passed by the respondent No.3, the petitioner executed an agreement consenting for acquisition of land subject to payment of compensation at the rate of Rs.9,51,786/- per gunta with all statutory benefits.

Though the agreement was executed on 13.11.2013, the respondent No.2 passed the impugned consent award on 26.08.2019, determining the compensation payable at Rs.414/- per square feet by treating it as residential land which runs counter to order passed by the respondent No.3 and the agreement executed by the petitioner.

7. Perusal of the order dated 19.10.1986 passed by the Deputy Commissioner, Gadag indicated that the petitioner had submitted an application for converting the land for industrial purpose and the same was acceded to.

However, in the order renewing the permission granted to divert the subject NC: 2024:KHC-D:3571 land inadvertently, it is stated that the petitioner is permitted to utilize the subject land for residential purposes, and the same was rectified by the Deputy Commissioner,
Gadag, in the order dated 03.11.2022.

8. The respondents having fixed the market value of the subject land at Rs.874/- per square feet by treating it as commercial land and the petitioner having acted on the promise made by the respondents that the compensation will be determined at the rate of Rs.874/- per square feet by treating it as commercial land, entered into an agreement consenting for the acquisition of the land on payment of Rs.9,51,786/- per gunta which comes to Rs.874/- per square feet.

Therefore the consent award passed by the respondent No.2 is contrary to the agreement executed by the petitioner and also the order passed by the respondent No.3 treating the subject land as commercial land and fixing the market value at Rs.874/- per square feet.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) The writ petition is allowed.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:3571 ii) The consent award dated 26.08.2019, passed by the respondent No.2 at Annexure-F in proceedings bearing No.S.A. (Bhu.swa.) / KSHP-II / 27-A&B / GadagBypass-2011- 12, is hereby quashed.
iii) The respondent No.2 is hereby directed to redetermine the market value of the subject land at the rate of Rs.874/- per square feet by treating it as commercial land and pay the difference amount to the petitioner with all statutory benefits.
iv) The said exercise shall be concluded within a period of four months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
